chunks: (Moses) said: "O Lord, as You have been gracious to me I will never aid the guilty."
ai.seo_question: What did Moses say about aiding the guilty after receiving God's favor?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights Moses' (AS) strategic gratitude; having been adopted into Pharaoh's household, he refuses to become a political ally to the tyrant, thereby preserving his monotheistic identity. This declaration marks a pivotal transition from passive upbringing to active prophetic mission, emphasizing that divine favor entails responsibility rather than mere privilege. The narrative underscores the principle of *Tawalla* (alliance with the righteous) and *Tabarra* (disavowal of the guilty), foundational concepts in Shia theology.
